request:
Checkpoint final worktree state without policing Agent Git history

## Problem

GitWeave currently validates more than the final assigned worktree state when checkpointing an Agent Node.

It requires the original workspace-base commit to remain an ancestor of the Agent's final HEAD and rejects worktrees whose index contains unresolved entries.

These checks make GitWeave judge the Agent's internal Git history and index state even though the core artifact contract is the final assigned worktree state.

## Expected outcome

Checkpoint the final assigned worktree file state with only the checks required to identify and capture that worktree correctly.

Do not require the original workspace-base commit to remain an ancestor of the Agent's final HEAD.

Do not reject the artifact solely because the Agent's index contains unresolved entries if the final worktree state can still be captured deterministically.

GitWeave should preserve the resulting artifact and provenance without enforcing a particular internal Git workflow.

## Context

The guiding principle is:

> Do not impose Git workflow correctness rules that are not part of the artifact contract.

If a concrete checkpoint ambiguity is observed later, address that case with the smallest necessary rule.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
